summary: Lookouts on Cooper Mountain from 1920; a 53-foot L-4 tower from 1939 was removed or destroyed in 1968, footings were there in 2015, and a drive-up road reaches the summit.

facts.design: Crow's nest (1920); log cabin (1927, burned); log cabin with 45-foot wooden tower and 7x7-foot cab (1932); 53-foot timber L-4 tower (1939)
facts.status_note: The tower was removed or destroyed in 1968 (sources disagree on which); footings were on the summit in a 2015 photo caption.

access.note: Drive-up route per Willhite, who visited in 2020; the last hundred yards can be walked if the ruts are bad. The sources read mention no gate or closure.

visit.trail_note: Route from the Chelan-Manson Highway north on Boyd Road to Cooper Gulch Road, following signs for the Echo Ridge Ski Area. The tower is gone, so there is nothing to climb.

events.note: Log cabin built; a forest fire later burned it

notes_for_editor: Rich record from four pages, two of them agreeing closely. Sources disagree on how the tower ended in 1968 (removed per the register, destroyed per FireLookout.com and Willhite); the story says so. A 1930 item quoted on the weebly page announces a planned lookout cabin on Cooper Mountain that fits neither the 1927 cabin nor the 1932 replacement exactly; it is left out of the story as unresolved. Do not confuse with Copper Mountain (North Cascades, Whatcom County), a different lookout. Access as public is inferred from a drive-up route in one 2020 account; no source mentions a gate or closure. The brief's county 'Okanogan/Chelan' matches the register.
